title: Naidu Says South's Share Won't Shrink Under 50% Lok Sabha Seat Rise
excerpt: Backing the Centre's delimitation plan, the Andhra Pradesh chief minister said South India's seats would rise from 129 to 195 while its 23.76% share of the Lok Sabha stays exactly the same.
body:
• Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu urged all political parties to back the Delimitation Bill, saying a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats for every state means no state loses its share of representation.
  • South India's seats would rise from 129 to 195 while its share of the Lok Sabha stays at 23.76%; Andhra Pradesh would go from 25 to 38 seats, keeping its 4.6% share, Naidu said.
  • The push follows the Union Cabinet's November 27 decision to clear a revised delimitation plan with a 50% seat increase across states and current inter-state ratios frozen until 2051.
  • Naidu linked his appeal to the 33% women's reservation, arguing that expanding the House is what makes the quota workable, and urged MPs to vote for the Bill in the parliamentary session at the end of this month.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and Telugu Desam Party president N. Chandrababu Naidu on Friday appealed to all political parties to support the Delimitation Bill, saying a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats would benefit everyone and protect South India's representation.

Addressing a press conference in New Delhi alongside Union ministers H. D. Kumaraswamy and Ram Mohan Naidu, Naidu said increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats by 50% would not cause injustice to anyone. He said South India, which currently has 129 Lok Sabha seats, would have 195 seats after delimitation, while the region's representation would remain unchanged at 23.76%.

The numbers Naidu put on the table

Andhra Pradesh currently has 25 parliamentary constituencies, which Naidu said would increase to 38 after delimitation, while the state's representation would remain at 4.6%. Karnataka's seats would increase from 28 to 42, with its representation unchanged at 5.16%, he said. He said the number of Lok Sabha seats would rise to 59 in Tamil Nadu, 26 in Telangana and 30 in Kerala, taking South India's total to 195.

Naidu said that under the previous delimitation, based on the 2001 Census, one MP represented a population of 19 lakh. That figure has now risen to 27 lakh, he said, adding that a fresh delimitation could ensure one MP represents a population of 18 lakh. A fresh delimitation was due by 2029, he said.

"This would not diminish the voice of Kannadigas in the Lok Sabha; it would significantly enhance their presence. The delimitation Bill will not cause injustice to any state."

— H. D. Kumaraswamy, JD(S) Karnataka president

Why the South feared delimitation

Southern states had feared that delimitation based on population figures could put them at a disadvantage despite their early efforts to control population growth through family planning. Citing a fertility rate of 1.6 against the replacement level of 2.1, Naidu said southern states were facing a similar situation, and that he had called for population management, incentives for bigger families and encouraging people to have more children.

Naidu said the southern states would suffer significant losses if delimitation were carried out based on the 2026 Census. "This could lead to unnecessary discontent and unrest among the public, and create challenges regarding political representation for both men and women," he said. Opposition parties opposed an earlier version of the Bill in the previous session; Naidu urged them not to repeat past mistakes, arguing that opposing the Bill would effectively hinder the representation of women.

What happens next

The appeal comes a day after the Union Cabinet cleared the revised delimitation plan, which we covered in our report on the Cabinet's decision to raise every state's seats by 50% and freeze the ratios until 2051. A previously introduced Delimitation Bill failed to pass for lack of the required majority. Naidu urged every MP to vote in support of the Bill during the parliamentary session at the end of this month, saying the time had come to fulfil aspirations for providing reservation to women.
